customer: Hi there, so I just moved to Texas a few weeks ago and I'm trying to sell my old station wagon before winter, but here's the thing, the odometer stopped working sometime last year and then my mechanic back home swapped it out for a different one, so the number on it now is way lower than what the car has actually driven. I'm not trying to hide anything, I just don't know how that works for selling it to you. Do I still get an offer, or does that mess everything up? Sorry, long story!
agent: No need to apologize, and thanks for being upfront! Per our article "Broken or replaced odometer," you can still sell it; just let us know about the replaced odometer when you request your offer, and at the appointment you'll mark 'not actual mileage' on the odometer statement, form NW-ODO-1. Cars marked 'not actual mileage' do receive a reduced offer, but if you know the true mileage, bring records that show it, such as service invoices from your mechanic back home.
